title: sock-mcp change: read the CLI config file (token, url, access_gate) when the environment has none
description: Lives in sock/mcp (no beads database there). Live check 2026-10-13 of the Codex plugin route (integrations-fwm): Codex starts a plugin's stdio MCP server with only PLUGIN_ROOT and PLUGIN_DATA in its environment, never the parent's SOCK_TOKEN, and the plugin mcp.json schema has static env only, so a plugin cannot forward the token by name and sock-mcp exits 'no token: set SOCK_TOKEN'. The sock CLI already keeps token, url and access_gate in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/sock/config.toml (mode 600 enforced). If sock-mcp falls back to that file when SOCK_TOKEN is unset, the plugin works with no secret in the plugin and one 'sock login' or config write per machine. Keep env precedence as today. Filed from the fwm live check.

title: sock-mcp change: flag to serve only the sending tools (outbound-only)
description: Lives in sock/mcp (that repo has no beads database, so tracked here). Integrations rule 2: a puppet has one consumer of its deliveries. Beside sock listen (runner/sock-runner) and in the Codex plugin, the agent must not see sock_fetch or sock_ack. Hosts enforce it unevenly: Claude via --allowedTools/--disallowedTools, Codex via config.toml enabled_tools, and the Codex plugin mcp.json has no tool filter at all. Add a sock-mcp flag such as --outbound-only that registers only sock_whoami, sock_list_conversations and sock_send; then the Codex plugin mcp.json passes it in args and the drift test pins the reduced set. Filed from the integrations-fwm review.

title: Package sock as a Codex plugin with a git-hosted marketplace
description: OpenAI now has one plugin system shared by Codex CLI, the Codex app and ChatGPT desktop (developers.openai.com/codex/plugins/build, learn.chatgpt.com/docs/plugins). Replace the manual codex/config.toml and hooks.json merge with a plugin: root plugin.json (name, version, extensions.com.openai), mcp.json (stdio sock-mcp), hooks/hooks.json, skills/sock/SKILL.md, and .agents/plugins/marketplace.json so users run 'codex plugin marketplace add guygrigsby/sock-integrations' and pick sock in /plugins. Public directory listing is out: it requires a remote HTTPS MCP with OAuth and forbids hooks (ewi covers a hosted variant). Verify the mcp.json stdio schema and the plugin.json path (root vs .codex-plugin) against the official page before building. Needs the u1q live codex check first.
notes: Merged to main at 0d46c6e as preview: hooks plus skill, installable with codex plugin marketplace add guygrigsby/sock-integrations then codex plugin add sock@sock-integrations (verified live on Codex 0.162.1). Still open: the plugin cannot ship the MCP server until sock-mcp reads the CLI config (27u) and serves send-only (qox); hooks not exercised live (untrusted plugin hooks are skipped in exec; /hooks trust is interactive); PLUGIN_ROOT expansion in a hook command unverified.

title: Codex and headless Claude Code inbound
description: No channel equivalent in Codex, and channels are ignored under claude -p. Options: Stop hook calling sock fetch (needs sock ack <ids> in sock-cli, loop guard via stop_hook_active, sender_id gate on owner_id), or sock listen --exec spawning claude -p. One consumer per puppet.
notes: Blocked on one change after the live checks: the documented claude default must be 'default' (or dontAsk), not 'plan'; plan denies sock_send even with --allowedTools. Also log the agent's last stderr bytes on a non-zero exit, and document the git-repo or trusted-workdir requirement and codex login --with-api-key.
close_reason: Done. runner/sock-runner reviewed twice, security findings fixed (d0893a7, 67238f6, bc87003), conformance tests in test/, live checks on staging passed for both claude -p (default mode) and codex exec (u1q). Codex app-server turn/steer live injection remains a follow-up.

title: Live check: sock-bridge against a real Managed Agents session
description: Like u1q for the runner. In a throwaway state dir with the staging puppet token: create an agent and a session on the Anthropic account (beta managed-agents-2026-04-01), run runner/sock-bridge with an owner message as sock listen --exec would, and confirm the user.message lands, the stream is followed to session.status_idle, the agent's text is posted to the owner (message id from sock send), nothing leaks (key, token, text) into logs or output, and a redelivery is answered from history. Needs Guy's approval to use ANTHROPIC_KEY_NON_CANON for session creation and a turn (billed).
close_reason: Passed 2026-10-13 against api.anthropic.com (managed-agents-2026-04-01) and staging sock. Environment env_01B5H2g41nV9xMDDR1ZJ98FP, agent agent_019QzD2Am63UHktTE7af6p1G (claude-opus-5-5, tools never), session sesn_01A5MEWLkkrzHwntXh4A9iLo. First delivery: bridge exit 0 in 3 s, log 'ran', the agent's answer 'bridge ok <nonce>' posted to the owner conversation (seq 10). Redelivery of the same id: 'duplicate', exit 0. Session events: user.message, agent.message, session.status_idle. No key, token or text in bridge output, log or state; the curl config was gone at exit. Session deleted (200); the agent and environment remain on the account (no delete endpoint used).

title: sock-mcp flag to serve only the sending tools (send-only mode)
description: Spec rule 2: Codex must see only sock_whoami, sock_list_conversations and sock_send. A Codex plugin's mcp.json (stdio schema: type, command, args, env, cwd only) has no enabled_tools, so the plugin cannot restrict tools; today only codex/config.toml enabled_tools does. Add a sock-mcp flag (name and semantics to agree with sock-integrations first, downstream of the tool contract; not a rename of any sock_* tool) that registers only the sending tools, then use it in mcp.json args. Do after sock-apple-y1t. Repo: mcp (no beads db there).

title: Live check: codex exec calls sock_send under default_tools_approval_mode=approve, and claude -p under --allowedTools
description: From the 5t4 runner review. Not run: no live model credential. Confirm (1) claude -p --resume ... --allowedTools mcp__plugin_sock_sock__sock_send --permission-prompts none can call sock_send under plan; (2) codex exec resume with codex/config.toml default_tools_approval_mode=approve calls sock_send (an open codex issue reports MCP calls auto-cancelled in exec because stdin is closed). Plugin tool names derive from the documented convention; a test guards them.
close_reason: Live checks done 2026-10-13 against staging in throwaway profiles. Claude 2.1.296: plugin tool names mcp__plugin_sock_sock__<tool> confirmed; --allowedTools lets sock_whoami and sock_send run under --permission-mode default (runner exit 0, message 01a13810-3c0e-76ef-adf0-6fe026bca3c6 sent); under plan, sock_send is denied even when allowlisted (plan blocks non-read-only tools), so plan cannot be the documented default. Codex 0.162.1: config.toml enabled_tools and default_tools_approval_mode=approve work, codex exec --sandbox read-only resume <id> - reads the prompt from stdin, runner exit 0 with message 01a1380f-cd10-715e-bfe3-e38ce46adb7e sent; codex ignores OPENAI_API_KEY in a fresh home (needs codex login --with-api-key) and refuses an untrusted non-git workdir without --skip-git-repo-check. Nothing leaked into runner output or logs.

title: Hooks: access_gate in CLI config.toml rides along to the plugin URL
description: cy4 unset ambient SOCK_ACCESS_GATE when the plugin token is used. The CLI also reads access_gate from config.toml and sends it as Sock-Access-Gate to the plugin URL. Needs a CLI flag or env to ignore the config file, or an isolated XDG_CONFIG_HOME that keeps url. Decide with sock-cli owner.

Also drop 'root := root' in TestToolNamesExist and send no params field instead of null in drift client.

title: Hooks: SOCK_ACCESS_GATE / config.toml access_gate ride along to the plugin URL
description: notify.sh pairs token with URL but the CLI also reads SOCK_ACCESS_GATE and access_gate from config.toml and sends them to the chosen URL. Unset SOCK_ACCESS_GATE when the plugin token is used. Lower value secret.

title: notify.sh: strip control chars before first redaction in detail path
description: Final review: notify.sh detail path redacts raw stderr before stripping control chars, then cuts to 300 bytes; a token split by a control byte can leak a short prefix. Fix: pipe head -c 65536 through tr -d cntrl before redaction. Needs sock stderr to echo the token, so near-zero real risk.

title: sock CLI retries unavailable until killed
description: notify.sh hook measured: 'sock send' retries unavailable forever (3 requests in 2s, 5 in 12s) until the caller kills it. Hook has its own 10s watchdog so it is bounded, but the sock-cli owner should decide whether send needs an overall deadline. Found during integrations Task 1.

comments.author: Guy J Grigsby
comments.text: Measured and fixed in sock/cli sock-cli-cu7 (cli commit on main): retries were already bounded (6 attempts, ~16s) but had no overall budget and no give-up message. Now: 60s budget, 'the server is unavailable: gave up after 6 attempts'. Close when you agree.

title: Hosted MCP surfaces: Responses API, claude.ai, ChatGPT, Managed Agents cloud
description: sock-mcp is stdio only. These need a public Streamable HTTP endpoint and an OAuth-style credential (Responses API takes an OAuth access token in the authorization field; sock_pt_ untested there). Multi-tenant token proxy and OAuth layer need a security review. Revisit with a real need.
notes: Public listing in the OpenAI plugin directory (developers.openai.com/plugins/deploy/submission, read 2026-10-13): org business verification (Guy started it 2026-10-13); one remote, stable, public HTTPS MCP server, auth none or OAuth (API-key and bearer unsupported); domain verification by serving a token at /.well-known/openai-apps-challenge; no hooks (plugins with hooks are ineligible, so the listed plugin is skill plus remote MCP only); listing metadata under extensions.com.openai.interface (displayName, shortDescription 30 chars, longDescription 4000, developerName, category, square icon 48px+, website, support, privacy and terms URLs); review package: 5 positive and 3 negative test cases, demo video URL, release notes, a reviewer account without MFA; one review at a time; later tool changes scanned daily. Technical prerequisite: sock-mcp served over Streamable HTTP behind OAuth on a sock domain (server side owns OAuth), with only the sending tools exposed.
